
CoAuthor is built for one family on one device, with no sign-up. This guide explains the profile your child uses and the parent area that sits behind a simple gate.

## The profile

The first time someone taps **Start learning**, CoAuthor asks for a first name and a class. That makes a profile on this device. All progress, XP and test results are stored under it.

![The profile setup screen: Quill waves above a card that asks for a first name and a class from 8 to 12.](media/profile-setup.png "Setting up the profile. A first name and a class are all it needs.")

- Nothing about the profile leaves the device. There is no account and no email address.
- The name button in the top bar shows who is learning, and opens the profile menu.
- If a profile already existed because your child opened a lesson link before setting up, the app keeps that progress and simply adds the name to it.

> [!NOTE]
> Today a device starts with one profile. If two children share a device, the simplest set-up is a separate browser profile (or a separate user on the computer) for each child, so their progress stays apart. Adding more children inside the app is planned.

## The parental gate

The parent area is behind a **press-and-hold** button: open the profile menu, choose **Parent area**, then press and hold until the ring fills.

![The parental gate: a card titled Grown-ups only, with a lock in a ring and a Hold to unlock button.](media/parental-gate.png "The gate. Press and hold the button until the ring fills.")

This is a gentle gate, not a password. It stops a young child from wandering in by accident. It is not meant to stop a determined teenager, and it does not need to: nothing in the parent area can hurt the child's progress except a restore from backup, which asks again before it overwrites anything.

When you are done, press **Lock** at the top of the parent area before you hand the device back.

## What is inside

| Section | What you can do |
|---|---|
| Overview | See how each child has been doing lately: time spent, recent lessons, things to notice |
| Progress | Lessons started and finished, test scores, XP earned each day |
| Practice | Build a practice test from a course's question bank, and see past attempts |
| Settings | Study goal, daily learning time, eye-rest break reminder, course sources, backup and restore |
